Step 3's freshness check compares the newest comment id against last_comment_id, so with that field never written, every poll reads the same comment as new and runs another round. set.body: In solutions/sol1_enhancer/.claude/skills/enhancer-loop/SKILL.md, step 0 lists <repo>/tickets/*.md and excludes *.ready.md, but not *.enhancer-candidate.md. Step 7 writes the doer's draft to tickets/<id>.enhancer-candidate.md and deletes it on both branches, so the file only survives a crash or an interrupt. The doer is told to keep frontmatter exactly, so the leftover carries state: draft and loop: enhancer, and the next all-tickets run treats it as a real ticket. Fix: exclude *.enhancer-candidate.md from step 0's glob. Found while porting the loop to Codex; the Codex port already carries the fix.

set.acceptance_criteria: With an existing GitHub issue for a ticket and no state file, one poll leaves a state file holding that issue number, and a following poll with an LGTM comment moves the ticket to state ready.
set.body: In solutions/sol1_enhancer/.claude/skills/enhancer-loop/SKILL.md, step 2 writes github_issue into the state file only on the branch that creates a new issue. When the issue is found by the gh issue list search instead, no state file is written. Step 1 then treats the next poll as a first poll, and step 3's first-poll branch skips the comment fetch entirely. A ticket whose GitHub issue already exists therefore never reads a comment, so LGTM is never consumed and the ticket can never reach ready. Reproduced on the Codex port against issue 1 of northwind-field-crm-test. Fix: persist github_issue as soon as the number is known, on the search path as well as the create path. The Codex port already carries the fix.

set.acceptance_criteria: Running task run -- --ticket <id> against a ticket whose frontmatter reads state: ready and loop: implementer creates no issue, posts no comment, and reports that the ticket is already done. A ticket whose frontmatter names github_issue reuses that number without searching, even when the issue is closed.
set.body: Step 0 of solutions/sol1_enhancer_codex/.agents/skills/enhancer-loop/SKILL.md filters discovery to tickets with state: draft and loop: enhancer. Passing --ticket <id> skips step 0 entirely, so a ticket already at state: ready and loop: implementer is processed again as if it were a draft. Observed live on 27 August 2026: T901 had reached ready, and its issue 8 had been closed by the human who approved it. Step 2 searches with --state open, correctly found nothing, and created a duplicate issue 10 for a ticket that was already finished. Two changes make this safe. First, steps 1 to 8 should stop for any ticket that is not state: draft and loop: enhancer, whichever path selected it, so --ticket stays a targeting flag and not a filter override. Second, step 2 should read github_issue from the ticket frontmatter before it falls back to searching. The frontmatter is written by step 2 itself and survives the state file being deleted on the LGTM pass, which makes it the durable record. gh issue list --search is also eventually consistent and misses recently created issues, so it is the weakest of the three sources.

set.body:
Seven inline commands across six files read 'task run, --ticket' where they should read 'task run -- --ticket'. Task rejects the comma form with 'unknown flag', so every one fails for an attendee who copies it. INSTRUCTIONS.md and the lab 1 fall-behind and prompt files are attendee-facing, and the seminar is Saturday.

Found while porting the enhancer lookup fix to Grok (#107). Two of the seven came from my own commit 358198e this afternoon, the rest are older.

Cause is a PostToolUse formatter on this machine. It rewrites a standalone double dash into a comma in markdown written through the Write or Edit tools, outside fenced code blocks. Inline backticks do not protect it. Edits made through Bash are unaffected, which is how this fix was applied.

set.acceptance_criteria: In solutions/sol1_enhancer_agent_sdk, every comment Gh.comment posts ends with the loop marker, and Gh.latest_comment skips any comment carrying it. A test drives the real jq expression over a payload where the loop's own comment is the newest, and asserts the human comment underneath it is what comes back.
set.body: solutions/sol1_enhancer_agent_sdk/enhancer.py posts every comment through Gh.comment with no trailing marker, and Gh.latest_comment reads the newest comment with a plain sort by id and no filter. The loop's own reply is therefore the newest comment on the next poll, and its id is higher than the last_comment_id the loop recorded, so the poll treats it as new human input and answers it. On a ticket that is green but not yet released this posts the same ask-for-LGTM comment on every poll, forever. The skill-based ports (sol1_enhancer, sol1_enhancer_codex, sol1_enhancer_grok_build) already carry the fix: every comment they post ends with an HTML comment marker, and the newest-comment query filters those out before sorting. sol1_enhancer_deep_agents now carries the same fix in Python. Port it back to the Agent SDK folder so the two runtime ports do not drift. Do not filter by comment author instead: the loop runs as the attendee's own gh account, so an author filter would also drop the attendee's LGTM.
set.title: Agent SDK enhancer answers its own comment on every poll
